userStories.title: nax-agent: tool providers on the native session
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Attach static ToolProviders to native sessions through the existing coding-tool runtime.

**Motivation** — The chat session path is the only one that cannot take a provider.

**Approach** — **1. nax-agent: `toolProviders` on `nativeBackend` (US-001).** `NativeBackendOptions` gains `toolProviders?: readonly ToolProvider[]`. `openNative` resolves them with the existing `resolveProviderTools(providers, SESSION_STAGE, ctx.workdir)` (skipped for profile `none`) and passes the result to `buildSessionToolSupport` as a new optional `providerTools` argument. `buildSessionToolSupport` then, mirroring what nax's `unionDeclaredTools` does for `nax run` (that helper lives in `packages/nax` and cannot be imported here, so the session path does the same union locally):

- unions the provider tool names into `declared` before computing grants, so `buildCodingToolSupport`'s `runtime.advertised(declared)` advertises them;
- passes `extraTools: providerTools.tools`, `providerIdByTool` and `providerInstructions: renderProviderInstructions(providerTools.instructions ?? [])` (when defined) to `buildCodingToolSupport`;
- returns `grants` = the profile grants plus `providerTools.grants`.

`openNative` uses `support.tools` as the coding tools exactly as today (no second append) and passes `support.providerInstructions` to `adapter.openSession` as its existing `providerInstructions` option (`OpenSessionOpts.providerInstructions`), which the native session folds into the system prompt. Rules:

- Only `kind: "static"` providers are accepted in this feature; a `discovered` provider is refused at option validation with `AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS` and path `backend.toolProviders` (MCP delivery to sessions is F5).
- Every profile but `none` attaches each provider whose `stages` contain `"*"` or `"session"`.
- A provider whose `tools()` throws is skipped (the existing `failures` list); the session still opens.
- An embedder tool and a provider tool may not share a name; the open refuses with `AGENT_SESSION_TOOL_NAME_RESERVED`.

**Scope** — In: NativeBackendOptions/schema, openNative provider resolution, session support union/grants/instructions and interaction delivery. Out: US-002 runCommand; US-010 skills implementation; US-012 chat composition; discovered-provider/MCP delivery in F5. Preserve existing embedder descriptors alongside support.tools. With providers absent, existing native-backend.test.ts and session-tool-support.test.ts assertions remain true; the API snapshot lists names only and NativeBackendOptions is already on it.

**Interface** — `readonly toolProviders?: readonly ToolProvider[]`; `providerTools?: ResolvedProviderTools`. NativeBackendOptions validation: each entry has a string `id`, `kind: "static"`, a `stages` string array and a `tools` function. `resolveProviderTools(providers, stage, workdir, options?)` -> `ResolvedProviderTools`; `renderProviderInstructions(entries)`; `buildCodingToolSupport(args)` receives declared, extraTools, providerIdByTool, providerInstructions and grants. Use public/local nax-agent modules, never import nax's union helper.

userStories.title: Skill and command parsers and scanners
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Parse skills and command files and discover them with deterministic bounded scans.

**Motivation** — Nothing in the repo reads a `SKILL.md` today.

**Approach** — Each parser returns `{ resource } | { diagnostic }` and never throws:

- `parseSkillFile(path, text, origin)`: `name` = frontmatter `name` or the parent directory name, matching `SKILL_NAME_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$/`; `description` required (non-empty string); `disable-model-invocation: true` sets `modelInvocable: false`; other keys (`allowed-tools`, `license`, `model`) ignored.
- `parseCommandFile(path, text, origin)`: `name` = file name without `.md`, same regex; `description` and `argument-hint` optional strings.

AC precedence for command hints: the literal frontmatter line `argument-hint: [msg]` must produce `argumentHint: "[msg]"`, even though YAML can decode unquoted brackets as a sequence. Preserve this command hint's bracketed text rather than discarding it as a non-string; do not change the US-003 rule rejecting a top-level YAML-list frontmatter block.

Scanners in `scan-dirs.ts`: `scanSkillsDir(dir, origin)` reads `<dir>/*/SKILL.md` (one level; hidden directories skipped); `scanCommandsDir(dir, origin)` and `scanAgentsDir(dir, origin)` read `<dir>/*.md` (top level only). A missing directory yields nothing; an unreadable file yields an `error` diagnostic and the scan continues. Entries are read in name order (sorted), so the cap and every shadowing winner are deterministic. Each scan caps at `MAX_RESOURCE_FILES_PER_DIR = 500` and adds one `warn` diagnostic when it truncates. File reads and directory listing go through `_resourceFsDeps` so tests can make one read fail.

**Scope** — In: parse-skill.ts, parse-command.ts and scan-dirs.ts implementing scanSkillsDir/scanCommandsDir; reuse US-003 frontmatter and origins, qualify plugin resources as <plugin>:<name>. Out: scanAgentsDir and other resource parsers belong to US-005; source packages belong to US-006; lookup/precedence belongs to US-007. The reference to scanAgentsDir above describes the shared scanner contract to be extended by US-005. Command files in subdirectories of `commands/` and `@file` references inside command templates are not supported; `@file` is sent literally. A skill's `allowed-tools` and `model` frontmatter are ignored; a skill runs with the session's tools and model.

**Interface** — `parseSkillFile(path, text, origin)` -> `{ resource } | { diagnostic }`; `parseCommandFile(path, text, origin)` -> `{ resource } | { diagnostic }`; `scanSkillsDir(dir, origin)` and `scanCommandsDir(dir, origin)` collect resources plus diagnostics using the US-003 types. No resource parsing exception escapes.

userStories.title: Agent, MCP and hooks resource parsers
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Parse deferred agent, MCP and hook metadata into catalog resources without delivering or executing it.

**Motivation** — One path, not two.

**Approach** — Each parser returns `{ resource } | { diagnostic }` and never throws:

- `parseAgentFile(path, text, origin)`: `name` and `description` required; `model` optional string; `tools` a comma-separated string or a string list.
- `parseMcpJson(path, text, origin)`: the `mcpServers` object; one resource per entry; `transport` is the entry's `type` when it is `http` or `sse`, else `stdio` when it has a string `command`; any other entry is a `warn` diagnostic and skipped. Text that is not JSON is one `error` diagnostic.
- `parseHooksJson(path, text, origin)` (a plugin's `hooks/hooks.json`) and `hooksFromSettings(path, settings, origin)` (a `settings.json` `hooks` key): one `HookResource` listing the event names (the object's keys); no `hooks` key -> none.

Scanners in `scan-dirs.ts`: `scanSkillsDir(dir, origin)` reads `<dir>/*/SKILL.md` (one level; hidden directories skipped); `scanCommandsDir(dir, origin)` and `scanAgentsDir(dir, origin)` read `<dir>/*.md` (top level only). A missing directory yields nothing; an unreadable file yields an `error` diagnostic and the scan continues. Entries are read in name order (sorted), so the cap and every shadowing winner are deterministic. Each scan caps at `MAX_RESOURCE_FILES_PER_DIR = 500` and adds one `warn` diagnostic when it truncates. File reads and directory listing go through `_resourceFsDeps` so tests can make one read fail.

**Scope** — In: parse-agent.ts, parse-mcp.ts, parse-hooks.ts and extending US-004 scan-dirs.ts with scanAgentsDir. Out: source-package discovery US-006 and catalog US-007; no subagent tool, MCP connection, hooks execution or user-level ~/.claude.json discovery. Preserve existing skill/command scanning.

**Interface** — `parseAgentFile(path, text, origin)` returns one resource or diagnostic; `parseMcpJson(path, text, origin)` aggregates per-entry resources/diagnostics; `parseHooksJson(path, text, origin)` and `hooksFromSettings(path, settings, origin)` return optional hook resources/diagnostics; `scanAgentsDir(dir, origin)` returns agents and diagnostics using upstream types. JSON parsers must represent multiple results where the spec requires one resource per MCP entry.

userStories.title: Discover Claude Code resource packages
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Discover project, user and enabled Claude Code plugin resources in precedence order.

**Motivation** — The slice-1 acceptance test is brainstorming and spec-reviewing inside the nax TUI with the superpowers and nax-spec-kit skills the user already has installed as Claude Code plugins.

**Approach** — **7. Claude Code sources (US-006).** `discoverClaudeCodePackages({ repoRoot, claudeDir })` returns packages in this order:

1. `claude-project` (root `repoRoot`): `.claude/skills`, `.claude/commands`, `.claude/agents`, `<repoRoot>/.mcp.json`, `hooks` of `.claude/settings.json`.
2. `claude-user` (root `claudeDir`): `skills`, `commands`, `agents`, `hooks` of `<claudeDir>/settings.json`. (User-level MCP servers live in `~/.claude.json`; F5.)
3. One `claude-plugin` package per enabled plugin. The enabled set is the `enabledPlugins` object of `<claudeDir>/settings.json` overlaid by the one in `<repoRoot>/.claude/settings.json` (a project `false` disables a user `true`); keys with value `true` survive, in user-then-project insertion order. Each key `<name>@<marketplace>` is looked up in `<claudeDir>/plugins/installed_plugins.json` (`version: 2`, `plugins[key]` an array of install records). The record used is the first with `scope: "user"`, else the first with `scope: "project"` whose `projectPath` equals `repoRoot`. Its `installPath` is the package root. The plugin name is `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`'s `name` when that file exists and parses, else `<name>` from the key. The package reads `skills/`, `commands/`, `agents/`, `.mcp.json` and `hooks/hooks.json` under the root.

Real layout observed 2026-10-25: `installed_plugins.json` `version: 2`, every record `scope: "user"`; superpowers 7.0.0 has `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `skills/`; commit-commands has no `.claude-plugin/` at all, only `commands/`.

**Scope** — In: claude-sources.ts calling the actual upstream scanners/parsers; preserve origin-bearing diagnostics even when an enabled plugin cannot produce a package. Out: merging lookups US-007, nax plugins US-008 and tool delivery US-010. Only default component directories; do not honor custom plugin.json component paths, settings.local.json, enterprise settings, pi directories, ~/.claude.json or marketplace operations.

**Interface** — `discoverClaudeCodePackages({ repoRoot, claudeDir })` -> ordered ResourcePackage[]. Failure rules: missing installed_plugins.json yields one warn when plugins are enabled; invalid JSON or version other than 2 yields one error and no plugin packages; an enabled plugin without a usable record yields warn `plugin <key> is enabled but not installed`; nonexistent installPath yields warn and skip; invalid settings JSON yields error and no hooks/enabled entries from that file while other resources continue loading. Use fixture trees and _resourceFsDeps rather than real user files.

userStories.title: Skills and command prompt builders
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Centralize skills index, user skill invocation and command argument text assembly in prompt builders.

**Motivation** — A declarative `resources` extension lets one nax plugin ship skills and commands the same way a Claude Code plugin does, with no new code-execution surface.

**Approach** — **10. Prompt builders (US-009).** New `packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/skills-builder.ts`, exported from `src/prompts/index.ts` (the prompt-builder rule: every model-facing text assembly lives under `src/prompts/builders/`):

- `buildSkillsInstructions(entries: readonly { qualifiedName: string; description: string }[])`: one paragraph telling the model to call `nax-skills__load` with a skill name before acting on a task a skill matches and to load a skill's `references` files with `file`; then one line per entry `- <qualifiedName>: <description>`, where the description has control characters removed, every whitespace run collapsed to one space, and is cut to 200 characters; at most `MAX_SKILLS_INDEX_ENTRIES = 150` lines, then `- ... and <n> more`.
- `buildSkillInvocationMessage({ skill, args })`: a `<skill name="<qualifiedName>" location="<path>">` block holding the line `References are relative to <baseDir>; load them with nax-skills__load and file.` and the body, closed by `</skill>`, then the args after a blank line when non-empty.

userStories.title: Deliver catalog skills through a static provider
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose skills and confined reference files through the reusable nax-skills provider.

**Motivation** — A native implementer told by `AGENTS.md` to "follow skill X" has no way to load it (its Read is limited to the workdir, and the skill lives under the user's Claude config directory), and loops into no-work fix rounds.

**Approach** — **11. The skills provider (US-010).** `createSkillsProvider(load: () => Promise<ResourceCatalog>)` in `packages/nax/src/resources/skills-provider.ts`, mirroring `packages/nax/src/forge-tools/provider.ts`:

- `id: "nax-skills"` (the `nax-` prefix, like `nax-forge`, keeps it clear of an MCP server the user names `skills`), `kind: "static"`, `stages: ["*"]`; `load` is called once and memoised.
- One tool, `localName: "load"` (advertised `nax-skills__load`). Input `{ name: string; file?: string }`.
- Without `file`: returns `Base directory for this skill: <baseDir>`, a blank line, then the body.
- With `file`: returns the text of `join(baseDir, file)` when `file` is relative, has no NUL byte, resolves (through `realpath`) inside the skill's real `baseDir`, names a regular file, and is at most `MAX_SKILL_FILE_BYTES = 262_144` bytes. This is how the model reads a skill's `references/*.md`, which its Read tool cannot reach outside the workdir.
- A skill with `modelInvocable: false` refuses the body fetch (no `file`) but serves `file` reads, so a skill the user invoked by slash command can still read its references.
- Errors (all `isError: true`, no throw): unknown name -> `unknown skill <name>; available: <up to 20 qualified names>`; a body fetch for a skill with `modelInvocable: false` -> `skill <name> can only be invoked by the user`; an absolute `file`, a NUL byte, or a path resolving outside -> `file <file> is outside skill <name>`; missing -> `skill <name> has no file <file>`; a directory -> `file <file> is not a regular file`; too large -> `file <file> exceeds 262144 bytes`.
- `tools()` returns `[]` when the catalog has no skill at all, so the provider advertises nothing; `instructions()` returns `buildSkillsInstructions` over the model-invocable skills, or `undefined` when there are none.

**Scope** — In: skills-provider.ts, resources barrel export, lazy memoized catalog and realpath-confined file loading with injectable fs dependencies; reuse US-009 builder for instructions. Out: session provider resolution US-001, runtime opt-in US-011 and chat wiring US-012; do not widen Read's workdir scope or interpret skill allowed-tools/model frontmatter.

**Interface** — `createSkillsProvider(load: () => Promise<ResourceCatalog>)` -> ToolProvider; tool input `{ name: string; file?: string }` and results `{ content: string; isError?: boolean }` using the existing ProviderTool contract. Tests run the provider tool against a fixture catalog/body and reference files, and assert instructions() contains nax-skills__load to pin the catalog and builder seams. The existing ToolProvider contract takes `workdir` in `tools(workdir)` and `instructions(workdir)`; AC mentions of tools()/instructions() are shorthand for calls with a fixture workdir. Invoke the tool through `ProviderTool.run(input, ctx)` and assert the ToolResult.content, not a SkillResource return. The callback named load in createSkillsProvider is the catalog loader, distinct from the provider tool whose localName is load.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the lazy skills provider to run dispatch only when resources.skillsInRun is enabled.

**Motivation** — A skills provider that works in `nax run` removes the cause, behind an opt-in.

**Approach** — **12. `nax run` opt-in (US-011).** In `createRuntime` (`packages/nax/src/runtime/index.ts`), when `config.resources?.skillsInRun ?? false` is true, `toolProviders` gains `createSkillsProvider(() => loadResourceCatalog({ repoRoot: workdir, config, env: process.env, naxPluginPackages: [] }))` after the MCP providers. `createRuntime` stays synchronous because the catalog loads lazily; the call goes through a new `_runtimeResourceDeps = { loadResourceCatalog }` in `runtime/index.ts` so tests can observe it. Run stages receive it through `buildRunDispatchOptions(ctx, params)` (`src/operations/call-run-options.ts`, whose private `runtimeDispatchFields` puts `runtime.toolProviders` first in the returned `providers`) and attach it under the existing `providerScope` rules (`unrestricted` attaches all; `scoped` only what the stage's `Mcp(nax-skills:load)` rule admits; `safe` none). nax plugin resource packages are not added in `nax run` in this feature.

**Scope** — In: runtime construction branch, _runtimeResourceDeps seam and actual runtime-to-run-dispatch wiring. Out: provider implementation US-010 and chat plugin catalog US-012. The skills provider in `nax run` does not include nax plugin resources; only `nax chat` loads nax plugins into the catalog. With resources.skillsInRun unset or false, runtime.toolProviders is exactly today's MCP providers, so every existing runtime assertion stays true. Do not hardcode new permission decisions or make createRuntime asynchronous.

**Interface** — Existing `createRuntime(config, workdir)` remains synchronous; new `_runtimeResourceDeps = { loadResourceCatalog }`; `buildRunDispatchOptions(ctx: CallContext, params: RunDispatchOptionsParams)` returns providers starting with runtime.toolProviders. userStories.title: Chat trust gate, plugins, catalog and providers
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Settle trust before composing chat and attach the shared catalog, skills provider and nax plugin handlers to every chat session.

**Motivation** — The codebase already has the pieces: `ToolProvider` (namespacing, per-stage attachment, provider instructions #2517, tool audit) used by `nax run`; the MCP pool and lock; the trust store; and the `loopHandlers` plugin extension modelled on pi extensions (#2288).

**Approach** — **13. Chat composition (US-012).** `chatCommand` (`packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts`):

1. After the existing TTY and mode checks, and before the `try` around `composeChat`, awaits `_chatCommandDeps.ensureTrusted(cwd)`, whose default is `ensureProjectTrusted(await normalizeTrustPath(resolveTrustRoot(cwd)), { interactive: true })` (the same steps `runTrustGate` takes, without its `process.exit`). A rejection with `NaxError` `PROJECT_UNTRUSTED` writes `Project not trusted: <root>` and the error's `context.hint` line to stderr and sets exit code 2; `TRUST_STORE_UNREADABLE` writes its message and sets exit code 2; any other rejection writes its message and sets exit code 1; nothing else runs in any of these cases.
2. `composeChat` then awaits `_chatCommandDeps.loadPlugins(join(globalConfigDir(), "plugins"), join(repoRoot, ".nax", "plugins"), config.plugins ?? [], repoRoot, config.disabledPlugins)`; a rejection writes `nax plugins unavailable: <message>` and continues with no plugins. Then `_chatCommandDeps.loadResourceCatalog({ repoRoot, config, env: process.env, naxPluginPackages: naxPluginPackages(registry.getResourceDirs()) })`.
3. `createChatHost` gets a new optional `resources` dependency (`ChatResources`): `{ catalog, toolProviders: [createSkillsProvider(async () => catalog)], pluginHandlers: registry.getLoopHandlers(), naxPlugins: [{ name, provides }] per loaded plugin, teardown: () => registry.teardownAll() }`.
4. `NativeChatHost` passes `toolProviders` through `openChatSession` (new optional request field) to `nativeBackend({ toolProviders })`, and opens every session with `loopHandlers` = the plugin handlers followed by the rule-delivery handlers (the order `configureRunRules` uses), one frozen array built once in the constructor. `host.close()` calls `teardown` once, after the session handle is released. The host exposes `catalog` and `naxPlugins` (both optional, undefined without `resources`).

**Scope** — In: CLI trust/error handling, plugin failure fallback, resource composition, ChatResources exported from chat/index.ts, optional host dependency/exposure, provider forwarding across start/resume/reopen and idempotent plugin teardown after session release. Existing cli/chat.test.ts dependency fakes gain resolving ensureTrusted, empty registry loadPlugins and empty-catalog loadResourceCatalog; every existing case keeps its asserted behaviour. Out: slash routing US-013, runCommand US-014 and listings/one-shot hooks notice US-015. An untrusted project exits; no restricted mode or catalog trust filter.

**Interface** — `ChatHostDeps` adds `readonly resources?: ChatResources`; `ChatResources` holds catalog, toolProviders, pluginHandlers, naxPlugins and teardown as above; `OpenChatSessionRequest` adds `readonly toolProviders?: readonly ToolProvider[]`; `ChatHost` adds optional catalog and naxPlugins. `_chatCommandDeps` adds ensureTrusted, loadPlugins and loadResourceCatalog. The US-001 seam is tested through createChatHost({ ..., resources }) WITHOUT an open override, then start(...), using _openChatSessionDeps.nativeBackend/createAgentSession/createFileTranscriptStore/resolveRuleSet stubs and fake storage to capture provider options. The US-008 seam is tested through chatCommand with a fixture resource directory and the real loadResourceCatalog, not a fake catalog.

userStories.title: Chat skill and command slash commands
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve catalog skills and commands after built-ins and turn them into builder-produced chat messages.

**Motivation** — Existing skills must work on day one.

**Approach** — **14. Slash commands (US-013).** `runSlashCommand` resolves, in order: the built-in commands; then `host.catalog?.findCommand(name)`; then `host.catalog?.findSkill(name)`; else `unknown command /<name>`. Plugin resources answer to `/<plugin>:<name>` and, when not shadowed, `/<name>`. A skill returns `buildSkillInvocationMessage({ skill, args: rest })` as a `send` outcome (also for `modelInvocable: false` skills: the user invoked it); a command returns a `command` outcome that `ChatApp` turns into `buildCommandMessage(template, rest)` (after shell expansion, US-014). `/help` lists the built-ins, then each catalog command and skill as `/<name> - <description>`.

To make that decidable, `runSlashCommand` (US-013) returns a `SlashOutcome`: `{ kind: "send"; message }` for skills and `/feature`, `{ kind: "command"; name; template; rest }` for catalog commands, or `undefined` for local commands.

**Scope** — In: SlashOutcome and runSlashCommand resolution, /feature outcome migration, ChatApp handling of send/command outcomes with buildCommandMessage, catalog-aware help. Existing slash-commands.test.tsx /feature cases read the message of a { kind: "send" } outcome; local commands still return undefined; every existing command keeps its behaviour and the built-in help list is unchanged for a host with no catalog at this story's boundary. US-015 independently adds /skills and /plugins to that list; preserve every pre-existing built-in in its original relative order when both stories are present. Out: actual command shell expansion US-014; /skills, /plugins and hooks notice US-015. Skills and /feature never become command outcomes; no interpretation of @file references.

**Interface** — `SlashOutcome` is `{ kind: "send"; message } | { kind: "command"; name; template; rest }`; `runSlashCommand` returns Promise<SlashOutcome | undefined>. Use upstream buildSkillInvocationMessage/buildCommandMessage, not prompt text assembled in the UI. Drive ChatApp with a fixture host catalog to prove slash routing actually sends the builder text.

userStories.title: Expand command shell lines through session runCommand
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expand shell lines only in catalog command templates through the session Bash capability, keeping approvals and cancellation interactive.

**Motivation** — One path, not two.

**Approach** — **15. Command shell lines (US-014).** `ChatHost` gains optional `runCommand(command, onEvent)` over `session.runCommand`; it routes `approval_requested`, `approval_resolved` and `question` events to `asks.handle` through a helper `routeAskEvent` extracted from `runChatTurn` (`src/chat/turn-runner.ts`), which `runChatTurn` then also uses. `runCommandShellLines(text, run)` in `packages/nax/src/resources/command-shell.ts` finds each `` !`<cmd>` `` occurrence (`COMMAND_SHELL_RE = /!`([^`\n]+)`/g`) in one pass, runs them in order with `run`, and builds the output by concatenating the literal segments and each result's `content` (no string-pattern replacement, so `$&` in output stays literal, and output is never re-scanned for shell lines). It returns `{ text } | { failed: { command, reason } }`, stopping at the first result with `isError: true` (reason = its first content line) or the first rejection (reason = the error message).

Shell lines are expanded ONLY for catalog commands, and only in the command's template before argument substitution: a skill body, a `/feature` spec, or anything the user typed as arguments is never scanned, so text that merely shows `` !`cmd` `` never runs it. To make that decidable, `runSlashCommand` (US-013) returns a `SlashOutcome`: `{ kind: "send"; message }` for skills and `/feature`, `{ kind: "command"; name; template; rest }` for catalog commands, or `undefined` for local commands. In `ChatApp`, `sendTurn` gains an optional `prepare: () => Promise<{ message } | { notice }>` that runs inside the existing `sending` window (after the `if (sending.current) return` guard sets `sending`, before `host.send`, with the one `finally` / `finishTurn`). For a command outcome, `prepare` runs `runCommandShellLines(template, (cmd) => host.runCommand(cmd, onEvent))` and then `buildCommandMessage(expanded, rest)`. Because it runs outside `keys.runControl` and inside `sending`, the ask prompt is active and Ctrl-C calls `host.cancel()` (which cancels the session's pending `runCommand`). On failure nothing is sent and the transcript shows `command /<name> not sent: !\`<cmd>\` failed: <reason>`. A host with no `runCommand` fails the expansion with reason `this session cannot run commands`. In `full` mode no ask is raised (the mode's `raw` approval).

**Scope** — In: host capability forwarding and shared ask routing; command-shell.ts and resources export; ChatApp prepare window, failure notices, interactive asks and cancellation. Existing turn-runner.test.ts assertions stay unchanged: asks still reach asks.handle and usage still reaches the ledger. Out: backend/facade implementation US-002; slash name resolution US-013; listings US-015. Do not expand skills, /feature, user arguments or returned output; do not add ACP host-side commands, usage or command transcript persistence. Command output inserted by shell expansion is still subject to `$ARGUMENTS` / `$1`..`$9` substitution in `buildCommandMessage`; a command whose output contains those tokens is not protected.

**Interface** — `ChatHost.runCommand?(command, onEvent)` delegates to optional `AgentSession.runCommand?(command: string, onEvent: (event: SessionEvent) => void): Promise<CommandRunResult>`; `runCommandShellLines(text, run)` -> `{ text } | { failed: { command, reason } }`; `sendTurn` preparation returns `{ message } | { notice }`. Route ask events both to the controller and caller event callback without introducing model turns or ledger updates.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Show loaded resources, origins, diagnostics and deferred capabilities through local chat listings.

**Motivation** — Existing skills must work on day one.

**Approach** — **16. Listings (US-015).** In `packages/nax/src/resources/listing.ts`: `formatSkillsListing(catalog)` prints one line per catalog skill, `<qualifiedName>  <origin label>  <path>`, the label being `project`, `user`, `plugin <name>` or `nax-plugin <name>`, then each diagnostic whose path is a `SKILL.md`. `formatPluginsListing(catalog, naxPlugins)` prints `Claude Code plugins` (each `claude-plugin` package id with `skills N, commands N, agents N (not delivered yet), mcp N (not delivered yet), hooks N (not executed)`, then its diagnostics, or `(none)`) and `nax plugins` (each loaded nax plugin name and its `provides` joined by `, `, or `(none)`). `/skills` and `/plugins` are built-ins that show them. The host's new `resourceNotice()` returns `hooks declared by <n> package(s) are not executed by nax` on its first call when any package declares hooks, and `undefined` on every later call; `ChatApp` reads it once at mount and appends it, so it does not repeat on resume.

**Scope** — In: listing.ts and resources export; optional host resourceNotice, mount-time notice, local /skills and /plugins built-ins and help entries. Drive ChatApp with a fixture host.catalog to prove listings do not send a model turn. Extend existing test/ui/chat/slash-commands.test.tsx for local listings/help and test/ui/chat/chat-app.test.tsx for the one-shot hooks notice across /resume; new formatting tests live in test/unit/resources/listing.test.ts. Update any exact built-in help list assertion in slash-commands.test.tsx to gain /skills and /plugins; every earlier built-in is still listed in order. Out: resource discovery US-006, composition US-012, catalog skill/command invocation US-013 and shell expansion US-014. Agents and MCP are only parsed/listed, not delivered; Claude Code hooks are parsed and listed, never executed.

**Interface** — `formatSkillsListing(catalog)` -> string; `formatPluginsListing(catalog, naxPlugins)` -> string; `ChatHost.resourceNotice?(): string | undefined`. Keep the hooks notice separate from the existing resume notice and count packages with hooks, not hook events.

analysis:
Repository exploration: codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host; direct reads and text search were used instead. This is an enhancement to the existing TypeScript Bun workspace, not a greenfield agent implementation. The binding fifteen-story structure and package scopes are preserved. F1/F2/F3 already supply the shared session, chat host and terminal shell. Only packages/nax-agent and packages/nax require implementation changes; do not change nax-ai or implement ACP commands.

Architecture and boundaries: sources -> ResourcePackage[] -> ResourceCatalog -> existing ToolProvider and chat delivery seams. packages/nax/src/resources does not exist in the inspected tree and is introduced by US-003. Claude project resources precede Claude user resources, enabled Claude plugins, then nax plugin resources. Discovery parses skills, commands, agents, MCP and hooks, but delivery is only skills and commands. No catalog trust filtering: settle project trust before loading config, plugins or catalog in chat. Preserve the all-or-nothing trust posture and existing per-session approvals. Root architecture guidance is docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:15 (module-specific standards), :106 (agent tool subsystems) and :168 (quick reference). Model-facing text must remain in prompts/builders; external fs, process and environment dependencies need injectable seams. nax uses Bun APIs; nax-agent shipped source is Node-compatible, uses #src imports and explicit .ts relative imports, and must never import nax helpers. Public nax-agent exports are named; test seams go only on ./internal.

US-001 impact: packages/nax-agent/src/session/native-backend-options.ts:18 defines NativeBackendOptions; :70 defines a strict Zod schema and :115 validates while retaining caller object identity. Add static provider validation here, with the exact backend.toolProviders path for discovered providers. packages/nax-agent/src/session/native-backend.ts:54 opens the backend, :72 builds session tool support, :86 constructs the interaction handler, :98 opens the adapter, and :116 builds codingTools from support.tools plus embedder descriptors. Keep the existing embedder append; provider tools must be included in support.tools exactly once, not appended again. packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-tool-support.ts:24 defines SESSION_STAGE; :30 declares profile tools; :143 builds support and currently derives grants only from profile declarations. Union provider names for advertisement but return profile grants plus provider grants without accidentally granting unrelated capabilities. packages/nax-agent/src/tools/provider-advertise.ts:94 already resolves stage matching, adaptation, grants, failures and instructions; :128 records provider ownership and :141 preserves tools when instructions fail. Reuse it rather than parallel tool plumbing. packages/nax/src/agents/coding-tool-support-resolve.ts:317 is the local union precedent, not an allowed nax-agent import. Regression coverage exists in nax-agent/test/unit/session/native-backend.test.ts, native-backend-options.test.ts, session-tool-support.test.ts and session-interaction.test.ts.

US-002 impact and concurrency: packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session.ts:69 stores active as ClaimedTurn; :99 send synchronously checks closed/busy; :126 answers asks; :130 cancels; :134 caches close; :139 aborts and awaits active.settled before adapter/backend cleanup. :191 binds asks to slot.turn. packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-turn.ts:47 defines LiveTurn and :53 ClaimedTurn; :204 claims a model turn with an event channel and starts on first pull. Do not reuse claimTurn for commands: it marks transcript turns and calls the model (:173). Widen the active claim shape, reserve it before any command work can overlap send, populate the ask slot, use existing timer seams, and clear all state in finally. packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-backend.ts:93 defines OpenedBackend; add only an optional method so ACP and handwritten fakes remain compatible. packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-interaction.ts:163 runs coding tools with call ids, abort handling, denials and AGENT_SESSION_TOOL_ERROR; :200 selects embedder versus runtime execution. Native runCommand must use that interaction handler, not spawn, an alternate Bash runtime, or a model turn. Important navigation correction: src/session/turn-event.ts:1 documents the event contract, but actual reusable redaction/cap functions are displayToolInput and toolResultPreview in src/native/session/turn-event-emitter.ts:77 and :90. Reuse those for command events so inputs and previews have identical masking and byte limits. CommandRunResult content is the runtime result, not the display preview. Export the type from src/index.ts and regenerate api/nax-agent.api.txt, keeping existing names. Existing ask/profile/backend/deadline session suites are regression anchors. Cancellation and close must settle even when an ask is unanswered; no transcript, model usage, turn_start or turn_end is generated. The spec explicitly excludes dedicated US-002 deadline/tool-error ACs while requiring those paths to reuse existing behavior.

US-003 through US-007: packages/nax/src/config/schemas.ts:523 shows the MCP default factory pattern; add resources beside other top-level blocks. packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types.ts:513 is the handwritten interface and :563 is the optional MCP precedent. packages/nax/src/config/defaults.ts:11 derives DEFAULT_CONFIG from NaxConfigSchema.parse({}); do not duplicate defaults. packages/nax/src/config/loader.ts:266 starts from defaults and :556 validates merged config, so use existing global/project layering rather than special loader semantics. packages/nax/test/unit/config/defaults.test.ts contains a handwritten NAX_CONFIG_KEYS ratchet that needs resources without removing any prior key. All sparse-config readers use the explicit optional defaults. Introduce shared resource types and a resources barrel, dedicated tolerant frontmatter parsing (not the rules-specific parser), deterministic sorted bounded scanners, and origin-bearing diagnostics. Missing directories are silent; a failed file must not abort the remainder. YAML syntax failure falls back to the line parser, whereas a successfully parsed list/scalar remains invalid. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and _claudePathsDeps.homedir isolate tests from the operator's installation. Discovery must reuse the upstream parsers against real temporary fixture trees, merge enabledPlugins with project false overrides, honor v2 install-record selection and default plugin directory layouts, and retain diagnostics even for skipped packages. The catalog must preserve loaded lists including shadowed resources, while lookup uses deterministic first-wins short and qualified maps. A shadowed unqualified project/user resource may lack a distinct qualifier; do not invent a new naming policy beyond the spec. Qualified plugin collisions likewise have no new resolution policy specified; keep deterministic package order and record any further hardening separately.

Add a data-only IResourceProvider, path validation and source-aware getResourceDirs. packages/nax/src/plugins/loader.ts:248 and :272 assert project trust before imports; preserve both backstops. :274 already computes resolvedModule, but :296 records raw entry.module; change only the recorded config path to resolvedModule. Existing validator, registry, registry-loop-handlers, loader-trust and index-exports suites cover adjacent contracts. The new extension does not dynamically execute resource files, honor arbitrary manifest paths, or load nax plugin resources into runs.

US-009 through US-011: packages/nax/src/forge-tools/provider.ts:44 implements a static ToolProvider and :57 supplies builder-made instructions, the reference for skills delivery. Create all skills/command text in prompts/builders/skills-builder.ts and export through prompts/index.ts. Provider catalog loading must memoize the in-flight result so tools() and instructions() do not independently scan. Reference access is a deliberate exception to workdir-only Read: validate relative/NUL constraints, realpath both root and target, check component containment rather than string-prefix containment, require a regular file and enforce 262144-byte maximum. No raw fs exceptions should escape a tool result. The 150-entry/200-character instruction index includes only model-invocable skills, while user-only skills retain reference-file access. packages/nax/src/runtime/index.ts:338 constructs runtime synchronously and :407 creates lazy MCP providers; append the lazy skills provider only when opted in, after MCP, via _runtimeResourceDeps.loadResourceCatalog. packages/nax/src/operations/call-run-options.ts:50 places runtime providers before call-local providers and :65 returns run options; do not add a second provider injection path. packages/nax/src/agents/coding-tool-support-resolve.ts:276 consumes providerScope, :279 resolves providers and :282 narrows tools for scoped rules. Reuse those existing unrestricted/scoped/safe rules instead of hardcoding a permission profile. Test the actual createRuntime -> buildRunDispatchOptions seam, not just construction. Defaults must leave every existing runtime provider assertion unchanged.

US-012: packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts:24 exposes dependency seams; :113 composeChat resolves cwd independently of repoRoot and loads config; :126 creates the host; :155 chatCommand rejects non-TTY and invalid modes before composing. Insert ensureTrusted after those guards and before loadConfig; mirror packages/nax/src/cli/trust-gate.ts:46 normalization and :51 refusal mapping without process.exit. Distinguish root in the trust error from cwd and never load plugins on refusal. Compose plugins, registry resource packages, catalog, provider and loop handlers, with a graceful empty-registry fallback only for plugin loading errors. packages/nax/src/chat/chat-host.ts:32 defines ChatHost, :48 deps, :92 creates rule-delivery handlers once, :133 starts sessions, :190 resumes, :224 reopens for mode/model switches, :259 sends, and :308 tears down after release via closeHandle (:69). Carry providers across every open path, combine plugin handlers before rules into one frozen array once, and add resources teardown to the existing idempotent close lifecycle. packages/nax/src/chat/open-chat-session.ts:21 exposes the real opener seams, :33 defines OpenChatSessionRequest, :118 builds options, :132 calls nativeBackend and :155 opens under a storage lock. Absent providers must omit the key, not pass undefined. Test via a host with no open override and the stubbed _openChatSessionDeps to catch broken forwarding. Preserve reopen rollback and lock ownership. Update existing cli/chat.test.ts fakes (:38) with resolving trust, empty registry and empty catalog seams so they never touch the real operator environment. Existing chat-host, resume and open-chat-session tests remain regression anchors.

US-013 through US-015: packages/nax/src/tui/chat/slash-commands.ts:21 stores the existing built-ins, :24 parses name/rest, :31 builds /feature, and :58 returns a string only for /feature today. Add discriminated SlashOutcome without changing local outcomes, preserve built-in priority, prefer commands over skills, and only consult catalog after built-ins. Update existing slash-commands.test.tsx /feature assertions to read .message; later /skills and /plugins extend help without deleting/reordering earlier entries. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/ChatApp.tsx:16 owns transient transcript state, :21 sending ref, :28 ask subscription, :38 submits, :49 runs local control commands, :57 starts the sending window, and :68 has the single cleanup path. Shell expansion must run in that sending window but outside keys.runControl so approvals stay interactive and cancellation treats preparation as running work. packages/nax/src/tui/chat/useChatKeys.ts:29 locks control actions, :64 handles Ctrl-C, :82 queues mode switching until finishTurn. Do not accidentally mark expansion as a locked control action, parse shell lines from arguments/skills/specs, rescan output, or use string replacement semantics that expand $&. packages/nax/src/chat/turn-runner.ts:35 consumes send, :41 routes ask events, :44 records usage and :58 updates metadata; extract only ask routing for shared use, without ledger behavior changes. Host runCommand does not update metadata or ledger. resourceNotice must be a separate one-shot resource notice, not reset when resume changes the existing interrupted-turn notice. Existing UI chat-app, slash-commands, chat-asks-keys tests and unit turn-runner tests cover the affected surfaces; add the specified new fixture-driven suites for actual slash -> host.send and slash -> runCommand -> send seams. Listings must distinguish loaded origins, diagnostics and deferred agents/MCP versus never-executed hooks.

Execution/migration: build US-001/US-002/US-003 independently; catalog chain US-004 -> US-005 -> US-006 -> US-007 -> US-008; builders US-009 after types; provider US-010 after catalog/builders; opt-in run US-011 after provider; chat US-012 after native provider seam/plugin resources/provider; slash US-013, shell US-014 after both command seam and slash, listings US-015 after chat. Optional fields preserve handwritten session/host fakes and sparse configs. No transcript schema migration, version bump or release is required. NativeBackendOptions is already a public name, so only the new CommandRunResult changes the names-only API snapshot. Add resources to the defaults key assertion and minimally update affected fake and /feature/help expectations without weakening prior invariants. Test fixtures use temporary Claude roots, real resource trees and injectable fs failures, never installed user plugins. Regression tests must be demonstrated failing against old behavior before implementation. Automatic package gates handle lint/typecheck/build; do not turn them into acceptance criteria or run bare bun test. Security-critical stories involving providers/permissions, sessions, trust, plugin path validation or reference containment use strict three-session-tdd; pure parsers/builders use ordinary TDD and non-security multi-module catalog work uses lite isolation. No tools are available here to execute tests or validate JSON through a shell; this drafting task writes only the requested PRD artifact. Design-doc changes and generated context updates are manual outside implementation stories; .nax is otherwise read-only to the implementation run.

Second-pass adversarial audit: enumerated all 206 explicit spec AC bullets in order within their original stories (US-001 through US-015 counts: 12, 18, 15, 14, 12, 17, 14, 13, 16, 16, 6, 16, 9, 16, 12). Every assertion and qualifying clause remains represented, including matching object shapes, table-driven cases, retained user skills after malformed settings, identical no-provider tools, same handler array identity, unchanged shell text, released-slot behavior and model-equivalent secret redaction. Compound bullets remain represented by their split assertions. Failure-table and cross-story seam assertions are retained in addition to those bullets; the US-002 dedicated deadline/tool-error AC exemption remains intact. All 20 feature-level out-of-scope items remain verbatim, and all binding ids, workdirs and dependency arrays are unchanged. Every critical spec-listed context file is present within the five-file cap, and no story lists one of its own new outputs as context.

Audit corrections: packages/nax-agent/src/tools/provider-types.ts:20 defines ProviderTool.run(input, ctx) returning ToolResult, while :28 defines tools(workdir) and instructions(workdir); qualified skills loading must assert content, not return a SkillResource. MCP entry tests now explicitly wrap entries under mcpServers before parseMcpJson. The command argument-hint AC requires the literal [msg] string even when YAML interprets unquoted brackets as a sequence, so US-004 explicitly preserves that AC without weakening US-003's top-level-list rejection. US-009 explicitly retains newline/tab word separators before removing remaining control characters. The existing redaction helpers were re-read at native/session/turn-event-emitter.ts:77/:90 and the US-002 description now points there rather than to the event type-only module. US-013's unchanged no-catalog help behavior is scoped to that story's boundary so it cannot contradict US-015's additive built-ins.

Regression/negative-path audit: each story has a directly observable negative or absence branch. US-009 explicitly tests missing positional arguments; US-015 explicitly tests absent hooks. Added narrow compatibility assertions for the pre-existing MCP schema default (schemas.ts:523), plugin loop-handler validation (validator.ts:41/:141), MCP provider ids/filter/order (mcp/provider.ts:57/:76), local slash undefined outcomes (slash-commands.ts:58), usage forwarding after ask-helper extraction (turn-runner.ts:44), and legacy help order with optional resource methods absent. UI listing/notice regression tests reuse the existing slash-commands.test.tsx and chat-app.test.tsx files rather than inventing a new UI harness. US-003 is medium/tdd-simple because its behavior is additive leaf parsing/config; US-010 is medium with strict security TDD for filesystem confinement; US-012 and US-014 are complex rather than expert because they integrate existing seams, retaining strict security TDD. No implementation sources were edited and no runtime test execution is claimed by this PRD audit.
outOfScope: Subagents (`agents/*.md`), the `Agent` tool, `/agents` and `agent.modelAliases` are delivered in F5; this feature only parses and lists them.
MCP servers from `.mcp.json` and plugins are delivered in F5 through the existing MCP pool; this feature only parses and lists them, and `nativeBackend` refuses `discovered` providers until then.
User-level MCP servers in `~/.claude.json` are not read.
Claude Code hooks are parsed and listed, never executed.
pi's Agent Skills directories (`.agents/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`) and pi packages are not read (user ruling 2026-10-25).

Claude Code plugin manifests that declare custom component paths (`commands`, `agents`, `skills`, `hooks`, `mcpServers` fields in `plugin.json`) are not honoured; only the default directories are read.
Command files in subdirectories of `commands/` and `@file` references inside command templates are not supported; `@file` is sent literally.
`.claude/settings.local.json` and managed (enterprise) settings are not read.
Marketplace operations (install, update, enable) are not provided; nax reads what Claude Code installed.
The skills provider in `nax run` does not include nax plugin resources; only `nax chat` loads nax plugins into the catalog.
A skill's `allowed-tools` and `model` frontmatter are ignored; a skill runs with the session's tools and model.
The `resources` block is not added to the root-only key pins and has no per-package (`.nax/mono/<pkg>/config.json`) semantics; the catalog is built once per repository from the merged config.
A `restricted` chat mode for untrusted projects is not added; an untrusted chat exits.
`runCommand` output is not written to the transcript and costs nothing; there is no `usage` event for it.

US-002 only: the turn-deadline and tool-error (`AGENT_SESSION_TOOL_ERROR`) paths of `runCommand` reuse the existing deadline and the existing `onInteraction` error mapping and get no dedicated AC; the cancel, deny and allow paths are pinned.
Command output inserted by shell expansion is still subject to `$ARGUMENTS` / `$1`..`$9` substitution in `buildCommandMessage`; a command whose output contains those tokens is not protected.
The ACP backend does not implement `runCommand`; a command with shell lines cannot run over ACP.
The design doc `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-24-nax-interactive-tui-slice1-design.md` §4.4/§4.5 update to this architecture is committed by hand with the spec, not by a story.

Updating `.nax/mono/packages/nax/context.md` and `.nax/mono/packages/nax-agent/context.md` to describe `src/resources/`, `runCommand` and `toolProviders`, then running `nax generate`, is a manual step after merge; `.nax/` is read-only to the run.
No release and no version bump.
